draft.title: Land rights and native title
card: Terra nullius

A Latin term meaning land belonging to no one. Before 1992, Australian law treated the continent as terra nullius when Britain claimed it, so it ignored the rights of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.
Native title
The recognition in Australian law of rights and interests in land and waters that Indigenous peoples hold under their own laws and customs.
Mabo

In Mabo v Queensland (No 2) (1992), the High Court rejected terra nullius. It held that native title exists in Australian law, brought by Eddie Koiki Mabo and other Meriam people of the Murray Islands.
Native Title Act
The Native Title Act 1993 (Cth) set out how native title is claimed and how claims are decided. It gave the common law decision a process in legislation.
draft.remember: Mabo recognised native title in law. The Native Title Act set out how to claim it.

a.q: What was the main effect of the High Court's decision in Mabo (1992)?
opts: It recognised native title and rejected terra nullius
It recognised terra nullius and ended native title claims
It created a process for lodging native title claims
It gave Indigenous peoples ownership of all Crown land
a.why: The High Court rejected terra nullius and held that native title exists in Australian law. Creating the claims process was the job of the Native Title Act 1993, which came after Mabo, so that option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what the Court said about the idea of land belonging to no one.

b.q: A group of Aboriginal people in Western Australia wants their rights to their traditional land recognised. Which law sets out how they can make a native title claim?
opts: The Native Title Act 1993
The Mabo decision of 1992
The doctrine of terra nullius
The UN Declaration of 2007
b.why: The Native Title Act 1993 sets out how native title is claimed. Mabo is the court decision that recognised native title, but a court decision did not itself set out the claims process, so it is the tempting wrong answer.
b.clue: Which one is a statute that sets out a process, not a court decision?

a.best: It recognised native title and rejected terra nullius

problems.detail: The Mabo line is garbled. 'It held that native title exists in Australian law, brought by Eddie Koiki Mabo and other Meriam people' reads as if native title was brought by Mabo. It should say the case was brought by Eddie Koiki Mabo and other Meriam people.

The clue gives the answer away. It asks which option is 'a statute that sets out a process, not a court decision', and only the Native Title Act 1993 is a statute, so a student can pick it without knowing the idea.

check.summary: The facts are correct. The Mabo line on the card is ungrammatical and reads as if native title was 'brought by' Mabo. The clue for question b names the answer by asking for the only statute.
